airfoils.name: NACA M-6
airfoils.use: Reflexed, pitch-stable section with small centre-of-pressure travel; candidate section for flying wings; used on the full-size Gee Bee Z Super Sportster (thinned to 8 % of chord on the Gee Bee R-1). Thickness 12.0 % of chord; trailing edge 0.52 % of chord thick.

source.author: Max M. Munk and Elton W. Miller, National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) Report No. 221, Table XXIX

airfoils.name: RAF 34

source.author: Royal Aircraft Establishment (RAE), United Kingdom; table in National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) Report No. 286, Reference No. 639

airfoils.name: S9104
airfoils.use: Heavy-lift and high-lift section. XFOIL (airfoil analysis program) predicts a maximum lift coefficient of 2.59 at 11° angle of attack and a Reynolds number of 200,000. Thickness 12.1 % of chord, camber 14.7 % of chord; thinnest point 0.26 % of chord at 91 % of chord.

source.author: Michael Selig, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
